change_summary: PLOS ONE has issued an Expression of Concern on this paper. It flags a possible discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 blot and a Fig. 7 that doesn't match its legend or text (no LSD1 siRNA data). It also flags missing control details and similarities to other groups' work that question the validity and provenance of the results. The authors did not respond. The paper is not retracted, but its experimental findings, and arguably the whole paper, should be treated as in doubt.
evaluation: Your draft cites Lv et al. [12] twice. In Section 2 it is background on higher LSD1 in tumours and shorter survival. In Section 3 it is the main evidence that LSD1 knockdown slows H460 migration, which you call "the clearest indication" and on which Aim 2 and H1 rest. The Expression of Concern says Fig. 7 has no LSD1 siRNA data and that the validity and provenance of the results are in question, so the Section 3 use is directly affected (medium). The Section 2 use is also touched but is only context (low). Your own Aim 2 design, with two independent knockdowns and a rescue, does not depend on this paper, but the rationale in Section 3 should be reworded.
recommendation: Hedge the Section 2 background use of Lv et al. and cite the Expression of Concern alongside it. Rework the Section 3 rationale, which leans on the Fig. 7 knockdown result the notice says has no LSD1 siRNA data, and replace that evidence with independent sources.

affected_parts.part: Fig. 4 (LSD1 Western blot in 293T, A549, H460 cells)
affected_parts.findings_affected: LSD1 is expressed at lower levels in A549 than in H460 cells, which is the basis for choosing overexpression in A549 and knockdown in H460.

affected_parts.part: Fig. 7 and the migration (scratch assay) results text
affected_parts.findings_affected: LSD1 siRNA reduces migration of H460 cells; LSD1 promotes migration.

affected_parts.part: Flag-LSD1 and LSD1 siRNA transfection experiments (Figs 5-9)
affected_parts.findings_affected: LSD1 overexpression or knockdown changes proliferation, migration, invasion and EMT markers; the controls are not described well enough to replicate.

affected_parts.part: Overall validity and provenance of reported results
affected_parts.findings_affected: The conclusions that LSD1 is overexpressed in NSCLC, linked to poor survival, and promotes proliferation, migration and invasion.
